correctness.rationale: For squarefree \(n=2pq\), the required omitted-divisor sum is exactly \(D=-pq+3p+3q+3\). Positivity excludes every \(p\ge7\). For \(p=3\), \(D=12\); all \(q\ge13\) are excluded because the only divisors below 12 are 1,2,3,6, and the remaining primes 5,7,11 are checked exactly. For \(p=5\), positivity forces \(q=7\), which fails. The two surviving identities are checked directly.

Its public three-prime computational data contains 30 and 66 but is presented as search output rather than a proof of completeness for squarefree 2pq. value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification at the first squarefree three-prime-support level beyond the published two-prime classifications. It explains why two early sequence values are the only members of this structural slice, replacing finite search evidence with a bound-free proof. The family is motivated by prime support and by the later authors' explicit three-prime computational exploration.
